question: A Canadian household includes a 27-year-old adult, their mother and their grandmother, all living together. Why is this classified as multigenerational rather than just a parent living with an adult child in Statistics Canada's 2021 Census studies?
generated_answer: The 2021 Census of Population defines a household as a person or a group of persons who occupy the same dwelling and do not have a usual place of residence elsewhere in Canada. A household may consist of one person living alone, a group of unrelated persons, or a family. A family is defined as a married couple, a couple living common-law, or a lone parent living with at least one of their children. A multigenerational household is a family household that includes at least two generations of parents and children living in the same dwelling. In the case of a 27-year-old adult, their mother and their grandmother, all living together, this is classified as a multigenerational household because it includes at least two generations of parents and children living in the same dwelling. The 27-year-old adult is considered a child in this household, and their mother and grandmother are considered parents. This classification is based on the definition of a multigenerational household in the 2021 Census of Population.
